morphology.compounding_rule: Norse dithematic ([quality|animal](stem) + element: Jarn-haugr, iron-hill; Svart-skogr, black-forest) layered over Woodland long compounds ([quality|feature] + place: Onekwenhtara-karhakonha, red-forest): the chief seat Vinheim (the vine-home), Kanata-by (the longhouse-town beside the Norse steading).
morphology.patronymic_form: the Norse settler-stock keep the dithematic name + -son / -dottir patronymic (and an aett lineage-name for the chief houses); the Woodland People keep the ohwachira (matrilineal clan, by animal-totem) and the clan-held name bestowed by the clan-mother (Iakoia:ner); the kinhold fuses both - a konungr who is also seated by the clan-mothers of the longhouse he was wedded into.

patterns.dungeons_ruins: fallen Norse virki and howes and abandoned palisade-kanata: 'the Howe of the [aett]', 'the broken Virki of [name]', 'the empty Kanata of [clan]', 'the Ghost-Longhouse'
patterns.military_units: the konungr's hird (sworn war-troop / comitatus) and the [clan-totem] war-parties: 'the Hird of Vinheim', 'the Wolf-clan warriors', 'the Iron-helms', 'the Hawk war-party'
patterns.ships: the longship and the forest river-craft, named in Norse kennings and Woodland totems: 'the Wave-Stallion', 'Raven of the Skogr', 'the Swift Heron', 'Forest-Shadow'
patterns.taverns: 'The [Adjective] [Noun]' and the longhouse: 'The Red Antler', 'The Boar and Oar', 'the Turtle Longhouse'

religion._note: Deity-names are morphs of the Agrippan canon - Norse reflexes PRIMARY (from family_germanic.json theonym_ancestors, the norse column), Woodland variants SECONDARY (from family_north_american.json theonym_sets.woodland; labial-free, matching real Iroquoian), never real Norse gods or real Indigenous powers. Shared pantheon, two registers. Alignment PROVISIONAL ([Neutral]): a settled frontier kindred - the Norse ancestor-cult (the deified aett-dead) and the Woodland clan-and-forest spirits both read Neutral; the great powers are invoked situationally at the hof-grove and the rite-longhouse rather than worshipped wholesale.

clergy_ladder.9: Allsherjar-godi (the supreme priest of the realm) / Kanonhsiyonni-tha (the council's high keeper)

religion.demon_epithet_pattern: the Chaotic powers, when warded, keep their morphs + a dread epithet: Maraxus -> Marhr the War-Brand (Woodland Waraksonon the War-Fire); Vacidus -> Vakr the Unmaker (Woodland Wasidonon the Devourer); Lusanto -> Lusandr the Hoard-Worm (Woodland Rusanonon the Greed-Serpent).

holy_symbol_motifs.Geyandr: a great oak rooted deep in the earth above the longhouse
holy_symbol_motifs.Orlund: an iron sword crossed with a war-club
holy_symbol_motifs.Thulr: a sun-wheel over the longship's prow

religion.religious_orders_pattern: the Hof (Norse temple) or Lundr (sacred grove) of [power] beside the Woodland Kanonhses (rite-longhouse) and the forest-grove: 'the Hof of Thulr', 'the Kanonhses of Tularonon', 'the Lundr of Geyandr'.
religion.saints_pattern: the deified aett-dead (the war-honored ancestors of the settler-houses, kept at the howe) and the founders of the kindred-peace and the honored clan-mothers and sachems, kept in the thing's recital and the council's recital; honored at the howe, the hof-grove and the burial-grove.

sample_deity_renames.Gaiandus: Geyandr (Woodland Kayanonon) - the enduring earth, the earth-holder
sample_deity_renames.Realta: Rjalta (Woodland Realwenne) - the mother, mercy, the clan-mother of the powers
sample_deity_renames.Tulrius: Thulr (Woodland Tularonon) - the sun, the day-keeper, justice

religion.the_one: Eitnir (Norse; Woodland Aterhonon) - the distant Ancient One, the Sky-Holder-Above, acknowledged but set aside, honored not petitioned

worship_by_alignment.Chaotic: Venerates the Chaotic powers of the canon, and names the Lawful powers - and Eitnir - as the tyrant-gods to be defied.
worship_by_alignment.Lawful: Venerates the Lawful powers of the canon - Eitnir foremost - and names the Chaotic powers as demons to be warded.
worship_by_alignment.Neutral: all powers ambivalent - somewhat honored, somewhat feared; foreground the ancestral dead (the deified aett-dead of the settler-houses, kept at the howe) and the Woodland clan- and forest-spirits (the karhakonha-powers and the clan-totems), with the thanksgivings to the growing things; the great powers invoked situationally at the hof-grove and the rite-longhouse rather than worshipped wholesale

titles._tiers_note: Norse clanhold ladder, ascending, with the Woodland sachem co-titles beneath. Hersir (local kindred-chieftain, war-leader of a district) barony over a Hersirdaemi; Mark-vordr (march-warden) march over a Mork; Jarl (earl, the great kindred-lord) county over a Jarldom; Stor-jarl (great earl, over-jarl) duchy; Fylkir (leader of a folk-host, a confederation of kindreds) principality over a Fylki; Konungr (king, raised by the thing and the kindreds) kingdom over a Konungriki; Yfir-konungr (over-king, high-king of all the kindreds) empire over the Stor-riki (the great realm). This is a kindred-king (raised and judged by the thing, not an absolute feudal monarch), NOT a feudal lord. The Woodland substrate keeps its own council beneath: the royaner / hoyaneh (sachems), the rotiskenrakehte (war-leaders), seated and deposed by the clan-mothers (Iakoia:ner). The godi (Norse priest-chief) and the rotihontsa (Woodland faithkeeper) stand outside the ladder. Rank titles fuse the real Old Norse and Woodland registers (allowed).
titles.display_policy: Ruler/domain titles shown in setting-gen, domain lists and vassal trees are ENGLISH (or an approved commonly-known foreign term where set in 'ruler'). The *_native conlang forms are for NPC DIALOGUE ONLY, never for structural/UI displays.
titles.government: clanhold (a Norse kindred-kingship entwined with the Woodland longhouse-clans: the konungr and his jarls at the crown, the hersar over the kindreds, the karls sworn to the hird; the thing counsels and the clan-mothers (Iakoia:ner) seat and unseat the chiefs, the Woodland sachem-council (royaner) endures beneath - kindred-and-comitatus bound, NOT a centralized feudal state)
titles.heir: Konungs-barn (the king's child, the throne-worthy heir; among the Woodland kindred a chief's seat is conferred within the clan by the Iakoia:ner, not inherited father-to-son)
